audit.whatIsWrong: The entire full layer tracks an ability called 'Twofold Hunt' and calls it 'her escape / her blink'. No such ability exists, and the thing it describes is not her Q either.
audit.why: Aurora's kit is Spirit Abjuration (P), Twofold Hex (Q), Across the Veil (W), The Weirding (E) and Between Worlds (R). Twofold Hex is a curse missile with a recast that drags the curses back through anyone in the path — it is her poke, not an escape. The escape is Across the Veil: a leap that turns her invisible on landing, 22s at rank 1 down to 18s. Tracking the wrong ability points the player's whole engage timer at the wrong cooldown.
audit.corrected: tldr, winCon, enemyWin, loading, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].t/.d, dosFull[2].d and report[5].t now name Across the Veil and Twofold Hex with their real cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer calls Twofold Hex a root ('eat a Q-root', 'her Q-root-into-burst', 'Root you with her Q-into-burst combo') and calls The Weirding a blink.
audit.why: Riot's Twofold Hex text has no immobilise in it at all — it curses on the way out and damages on the recast. Riot's The Weirding text is 'damages and slows enemies before Aurora hops backward to safety'. Telling a melee player to expect a root changes when she commits her dash and gets her killed for nothing.
audit.corrected: whys[3], wants.foe[1] and wants.foe[2] now describe the curse-and-recast and name the leap and the hop-back correctly.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2's 'why' claimed 'dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade', which is not something Ambessa's passive does, and Level 1's was the generic 'identify how Aurora contests the first waves'.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step gives bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund; Repudiation is her only shield. The real shape of the first levels is that Ambessa has one 70-energy ability and no dash threat while Twofold Hex pokes free, and that Across the Veil at 22s is the clock the whole lane runs on.
audit.corrected: phases[0].why and phases[1].why now state the real early shape and the 22s leap.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 line was the generic 'the R lock isolates and finishes the chain' and never mentioned Between Worlds.
audit.why: Between Worlds is 140s at rank 1 and creates an area she can teleport across from one side to the other — it is a second escape stacked on top of Across the Veil, and it is why a whiffed Public Execution at 6 costs Ambessa the fight rather than trading.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names both ultimates and what each is actually for.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer mentioned anti-heal, and Spirit Abjuration was never named.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Aurora's spells and attacks exorcise spirits from the enemies she damages. Exorcised spirits follow Aurora around and heal her.' She heals off the poke she is already throwing, so Grievous Wounds is what makes Ambessa's chip stick between all-ins.
audit.corrected: report[8].t adds Oblivion Orb against Spirit Abjuration; wants.foe[0] states that she heals her own poke back.

notes: The full layer for this matchup tracked a non-existent ability called 'Twofold Hunt' in eight separate fields; I replaced it wherever the field was worth rewriting. Duplicate renderings still carry it — breakdown.mid, breakdown.trading / report[3], report[9], report[10], report[12] and report[13] are the same boilerplate sentences repeated and all need the same substitution to Across the Veil. The content layer separately calls Twofold Hex a root three times; Riot's text has no immobilise on it, and I corrected the three fields I edited. Ambessa's kit file flags grounding on Repudiation and grounding plus heal on Public Execution; Riot's descriptions contain none of that, so I made no such claim, which matters here because a reader might otherwise think W denies Across the Veil.
